sentences.text: Shri Pradeep Kumar Naveria - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Amit Pandey - Govt. Advocate for respondent-State.
Shri Kapil Dayal Gupta - Advocate for respondent no.2/objector.

Appellant - Rahul Patel has filed fourth application i.e. I.A.No.17366/2025 under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973/Section 430 for the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 450, 376 of IPC & Section 3(2)(v) of SC & ST (POA)
Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years, R.I. for 10 years and R.I. for life with fine of Rs.1000/-, Rs.2000/- and Rs.2000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
3.
Learned counsel appearing for appellant submitted that prosecutrix was consenting party.
Appellant has falsely been implicated in the case.
He entered the house with consent and on a call of prosecution.
It is submitted that when he was seen along with prosecutrix by family members, he was beaten up and was handed over to Police.
It is submitted that appellant is in jail for about 6 years.
In these circumstances, he may be released on bail and sentence may be suspended.
4. Govt. Advocate appearing for State opposed the prayer and submitted that direct evidence is available against the appellant.
Prosecutrix 2 CRA-6521-2021 has resisted the act of appellant and had received injuries on her body.
It cannot be said that prosecutrix was consenting party.
Trial Court has rightly convicted and sentenced the appellant.

5. Heard learned counsel for parties.
6.

On going through records of the case, it is found that letters of prosecutrix were placed on record,
which are exhibited as D/2, D/3 and D/4.

Aforesaid letters show that there may be love relationship Rahul Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123739494/
1 between appellant and prosecutrix.

sentences.text: 7. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, I.A.No.17366/2025 is allowed.

8. It is hereby directed that the custodial sentence awarded to appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 16.06.2026 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard till final disposal of this appeal.
9. Certified copy as per rules.
